findings.comment: Large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) are not differentiated on the landscape plan to allow verification of clearances from overhead electric facilities. The plant schedule on Sheet 35 lists mature heights (e.g., Cedar Elm, Live Oak specifications with container sizes indicating mature trees), but the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not show these heights or indicate which tree symbols represent large trees. All tree symbols appear as identical generic circles with only category labels (M, PL), providing no visual differentiation of size. Without height notation on the landscape plan, reviewers and inspectors cannot identify which trees are subject to the stricter 25-foot (distribution) or 50-foot (transmission) large-tree clearance requirements. Applicant must provide: (1) notation of mature height on each tree symbol on landscape plan, or (2) distinct symbol types or colors to differentiate large trees (40+ feet) from other trees, or (3) clear legend showing which species in the plant schedule meet the large-tree threshold and marking those trees accordingly on the landscape plan.

findings.comment: Large trees (mature height 40+ feet) may be proposed within 50 lateral feet of overhead electric transmission conductor. Compliance cannot be verified due to three factors: (1) OHE voltage not specified, so transmission applicability unknown; (2) landscape plan does not differentiate tree sizes or show mature heights; (3) clearance distances from conductor not measured. Applicant must provide: (1) OHE voltage classification; (2) mature height notation for trees on landscape plan keyed to ECM Appendix F; (3) measured clearances if transmission voltage confirmed.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along OHE line

findings.comment: Transmission structures confirmed to be addressed in general notes (Sheet 3, Block 13). However, whether the OHE line on landscape plan represents transmission or distribution voltage is not specified. Without voltage classification and without species identification of specific trees, compliance with 50-foot transmission clearance for large trees cannot be assessed.
applicableAreas: Site-wide overhead electric transmission facilities

findings.comment: Trees may be proposed within transmission easement boundaries. Compliance cannot be verified because transmission easement boundaries are not clearly shown or labeled on the landscape plan (Sheet 31). The grading plan (Sheet 11) indicates that easements (including electric easements) are depicted, but the specific type (transmission vs. distribution), location, and boundaries are not clearly marked with dimensions or notes tied to the landscape plan. The existing OHE line is shown as a dashed line on Sheet 31 but is not explicitly identified as being within or outside a transmission easement boundary. Applicant must provide: (1) transmission easement boundaries clearly identified and dimensioned on landscape plan; (2) verification that no trees are shown within any transmission easement.
applicableAreas: Potential transmission easement areas on site

findings.comment: Grading plan indicates a transmission easement is addressed in the design (evidenced by Electric Transmission Notes on Sheet 3). However, the exact boundaries of the transmission easement are not clearly delineated on the landscape plan in relation to proposed tree locations. Without explicit transmission easement boundary marking on the landscape plan, the specific locations of any trees within the easement cannot be confirmed.
applicableAreas: Transmission easement boundaries on site, if present

findings.comment: Transformer pads are shown on Sheet 21 and Sheet 9, but no horizontal clearance dimensions are labeled from pad edges to building structures. Visual estimates suggest pads are positioned 10-25 feet from nearest building edges, which would meet the minimum 5-foot requirement, but exact dimensions are not provided on the plans for verification.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations (northwest, west-central, east-central, south-central)

findings.comment: Transformer pads shown on Electrical Plan (Sheet 21) in proximity to buildings but clearance dimensions not provided. Minimum 5-foot clearance from buildings cannot be verified from submitted plans.
applicableAreas: five transformer pad locations shown on Electrical Plan

findings.comment: Fences are shown on the site plan (pond perimeter fence, wood fence on east boundary, pond access gates), but exact locations relative to transformer pads, access door orientations, and specific clearance distances are not dimensioned. Cannot verify compliance with 5-foot (for sides with operators/controls) or 3-foot (for sides without operators/controls) clearances without access door orientation documentation.

findings.comment: Site plan does not show fences or gates adjacent to transformer pads with marked clearance dimensions. Access door orientation for each pad not indicated on electrical plan, preventing verification of required 5-foot (operators/controls) vs. 3-foot (no operators/controls) clearances to removable ventilated fences.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations

findings.comment: No clearance dimensions are shown on the plans. Without documented clearance values, cannot determine whether any pads use reduced 3-foot clearances (which would require Austin Energy Design written approval and verification of four specific conditions: not in confined space, 10 ft+ to windows/doors/ducts, 15 ft+ vertical clearance, and 3-hour fire rating). No Austin Energy Design written approvals or architectural fire rating specifications are provided.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations

findings.comment: Transformer Pad 3 is located approximately 4-6 feet from Building 8 wall. If this represents a reduced clearance from the standard 5-foot minimum, written Austin Energy Design approval would be required, along with documentation that: (1) location is not in confined space, (2) minimum 10 feet to windows/doors/ducts, (3) minimum 15 feet vertical clearance to windows/doors/ducts, and (4) minimum 3-hour fire rating. No such approval or supporting documentation visible on submitted plans.
applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 (closest to building at ~4-6 feet)

findings.comment: Sidewalks are shown on Sheets 9 and 21, and several transformer pads are adjacent to sidewalk areas (particularly TP1 and TP2 on the western side). However, no specific clearance dimensions from the back of sidewalk to pad edges are labeled.

findings.comment: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not identify the species of trees proposed near electric facilities. The plant schedule on Sheet 35 clearly lists tree species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) with botanical names and specifications. However, the landscape plan symbols show only generic circles with category labels (M=mitigation, PL=parking lot, SYM) with no reference to the plant schedule or species identification. The tree symbols cannot be traced to specific species. This violates the requirement that trees shown on plans be identified. Applicant must provide: (1) landscape plan tree symbols keyed to plant schedule with species callouts; (2) for trees near electric facilities, species label on each symbol or clear legend cross-referencing symbols to species names.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan (Sheet 31)

These specifications and approvals are not visible in the submitted electrical, architectural, or specification documentation.

findings.comment: All transformer pads must be located 100% on private property. Pads 1-5 shown on electrical plan within the private site boundaries. However, the site plan references record easements (see facts.md) including: Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (0.31 ac, NE interior, no-build), City of Austin Drainage Easement (0.130 ac, NE corner), 25' Drainage Easement, 7.5' Public Utility Easement, and 5' Electric Easements.
